findings.issue: The app ships no test script, runner, or single test file; all verification was delegated to the harness's acceptance suite.
findings.suggestion: Add vitest and a `test` script; the pure helpers in src/lib/ need no browser or server and can be covered in an hour.

findings.issue: Filtering, page clamping (page past pageCount, page=0/non-numeric), zero-match handling and 48-per-page slicing are untested; these are the most regression-prone lines in the app.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test browse() against a synthetic SpeciesIndex: filters, combined filters, empty results, boundary pages, and that state.page is clamped.

findings.issue: Move-table construction (dedup key, method rank order, level-then-name sort, null level) has no guard; a reorder or a bad dedup would ship.
findings.suggestion: Extract moveRows' pure assembly from the fetch loop (it currently awaits inside) and test table order, dedup and level ordering with fixture records.

findings.issue: URL state round-trip (omitting empty/default params, reset-to-page-1 on filter change, push vs replace, popstate sync) is only exercised by the specific URLs the acceptance suite uses.
findings.suggestion: Test stateToSearch/stateFromParams as a property-style round-trip, and assert the client resets page on type/generation change (currently implicit in controlsState at line 55-60).

findings.issue: cardsFor's alternate-form exclusion (id <= 10000), dedup, dex sort and species-name fallback are unguarded; this is the exact 'refactor the data layer' code the spec's live-data overlay targets.
findings.suggestion: Fixture-test with mixed default/alternate form refs, duplicates, and a species id absent from the species map.

findings.issue: sortTable's missing-values-last-in-both-directions invariant (sign deliberately not applied to the empty branch, line 20) and aria-sort toggling have no regression net.
findings.suggestion: Add a small jsdom/DOM test that sorts a table with null power both ways and asserts row order and aria-sort attributes.

findings.issue: Species index assembly (type slots ordered by slot, generation assignment, 18-type filtering via EXCLUDED_TYPES) feeds both the home route and /api/species-index with no tests.
findings.suggestion: Test getSpeciesIndex with stubbed API fixtures, asserting slot order, exclusion of stellar/unknown/shadow, and generation tagging.

findings.issue: latestFlavorText (last English entry, whitespace collapse) and orDash (0 must not render as —) are subtle and untested.
findings.suggestion: Table-driven unit tests for format.ts; these are the cheapest, highest-signal tests in the codebase.

findings.issue: Cache TTL/eviction and the getByName slug guard (empty, uppercase, non-slug names) are untested; a stricter or looser regex would change 404 behaviour silently.
findings.suggestion: Test the slug regex and that 404 responses resolve to null while other errors throw ApiError.

findings.issue: Game-switch fetch-and-replace with ticket-based race handling and popstate fallback is untestable by the acceptance suite and untested here; out-of-order responses could render stale tables.
findings.suggestion: Extract showGame's DOM-swap into a testable function and stub fetch; at minimum, a smoke test that rapid game switches converge on the last selection.

summary: The app contains no tests of its own — no runner, no test script, no spec files — so the entire ~740 LOC of data transformation, filtering, pagination and URL-state logic is guarded only by the external acceptance suite. The code is fortunately well factored (pure helpers in src/lib separate from Lit templates and I/O), which makes the gap cheap to close, but as merged it would be rejected on test quality alone. Highest-value targets: browse(), moveRows(), cardsFor(), format.ts, and the client sortTable logic.
